Puerto Nariño · Colombian Amazon

Canoeing in flooded Amazon forest

Paddle among forest trees when water levels make this watery landscape accessible.

Ask Amaru on WhatsApp ↗

About this experience

Explore a flooded-forest setting in a canoe, with natural channels, trees and vegetation close to the water. This experience depends on water levels and local conditions, so the route and possibility of going ahead need confirmation for your dates. Paddling requires coordination, balance and some arm and shoulder endurance. It is offered separately from Kaya daytime kayaking.

In parts of the Amazon, higher water transforms the relationship between forest and river. Trees and vegetation surround the canoe, offering a different view from a dry-ground walk. The water level determines what is possible, so this experience is planned around conditions rather than a fixed promise of access.

Destination context sources: Parques Nacionales ↗

What to explore

  • Canoeing in a flooded-forest setting
  • Water levels and route confirmed for your dates
  • Moderate effort involving paddling and balance

Levels are indicative. Terrain, water levels, weather and your group can change the demands of an outing.

Wear clothes that can get wet and protect electronics. Share your paddling experience and discuss the current, boarding, equipment and effort needed. The possibility of a flooded-forest route depends on water levels; it is not a fixed year-round itinerary.

What should I confirm?

Ask about the route, departure, group requirements, guide language, equipment, transport and what is included. Share your dates and number of travellers, and review the full price and cancellation conditions before confirming anything.

Routes depend on water levels, weather and local conditions. Wildlife sightings cannot be guaranteed.
